scope.flow: Blacklisted user unstakes iTRY through UnstakeMessenger; cross-chain message reaches hub, iTryTokenOFT._lzReceive() calls _credit()/_mint(), which triggers _beforeTokenTransfer() and reverts, leaving the 100 iTRY locked in iTryTokenOFTAdapter with no rescue mechanism.
scope.environment: Brix Money cross-chain iTRY/wiTRY contracts: UnstakeMessenger.sol, wiTryVaultComposer, StakediTryCrosschain, iTryTokenOFTAdapter, iTryTokenOFT.sol
evidence: Blacklisted users can call unstake() and lock the funds in the adapter forever.
``_beforeTokenTransfer()`` in ``iTryTokenOFT.sol`` prevents ``blacklisted`` users from transferring any token:
``unstake()`` on ``unstakeMessenger.sol`` can be called even by ``blacklisted`` users.
The whole flow works as follows:
1. Blacklisted user Alice completes cooldown for ``100`` iTRY tokens.
- Pays 0.1 ETH total (0.05 for spoke→hub, 0.05 for return) │
This is how ``unstake()`` of ``unstakeMessenger.sol`` calls ``_beforeTokenTransfer()`` on ``iTryTokenOFT.sol``.
Now the main problem is when our ``_credit()`` fails due to ``blacklisted``,  our ``100 iTRY`` tokens are still locked in ``iTryTokenOFTAdapter()`` with no ``rescue`` mechanism.
Similar to ``wiTRYOFT.sol``, ``_mint`` the funds to ``owner()`` when blacklisted users transfer:

statements.text: LayerZero Endpoint calls wiTryVaultComposer._lzReceive(), which decodes the message and calls _handleUnstake(); StakediTryCrosschain.unstakeThroughComposer(Alice) is called and _handleUnstake() continues, calling iTryTokenOFTAdapter.send().
LayerZero Endpoint delivers the message; iTryTokenOFT._lzReceive() executes and _credit() calls _mint().

_beforeTokenTransfer() in iTryTokenOFT.sol prevents blacklisted users from transferring any token, so the _mint() triggered by _credit() calls _beforeTokenTransfer() which reverts, and the 100 iTRY tokens remain locked in iTryTokenOFTAdapter with no rescue mechanism.
